II. GENERAL CORRIDOR FEATURES
Physical Characteristics
The surface tonography of Milwaukee County has been primarily determined by placiation. Most of the area has low tonography and slopes are dominately from near level to rolling. The low topography is generally associated with ground moraines and the rolling topography associated with terminal moraines.
Within the county the Milwaukee and Menomonee Rivers join and flow to Lake Michigan. The Root River drains the southwest corner of the county through Racine County to Lake Michigan. All streams in the county drain to Lake Michigan.
The topography in the vicinity of the study area is fairly flat near Lake Michigan and slowly changes to gently rolling slopes to the west. Existing ground elevations above sea level ranges from 650 feet near the lake to 750 feet at I-94 directly west of the airport. General Mitchell Field generally lies between 2 to 3 1/2 miles west of Lake Michigan, and extends just north of Layton Avenue and south to Rawson Avenue a distance of approximately 3 1/2 miles. Figure 9 presents a USGS Topographic map of the area in the vicinity of the airport.
The topography of the area will not be a significant factor in the determination of an air quality analysis except for the climatic influence of Lake Michigan.
